account:
It is day 1 at ten o'clock, and I have reached the mill for my scheduled grain inspection. I need to ask the miller about stock quantities, storage conditions, and supply concerns, then record actual findings; I have not received any figures yet. The secretary reported no new correspondence this morning and has recorded an addendum confirming my eighteen hundred great hall lighting inspection with the builder. The builder requested that visit to check completed work. My remaining appointments include lunch at home, council letters at thirteen hundred, tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage at fifteen hundred, and office time at sixteen-thirty.

The unusual thing is that two townsfolk near the mill have just said the identical fragment, 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Other townsfolk were speaking nearby, but I could not make out their words. This may be a rumour spreading through conversations, possibly about some proposed change involving the crossing or port, but the fragment does not establish what is proposed or why the bakery is mentioned. Yesterday's grain brief explicitly said that the neighbour's related rumour was unconfirmed and that the secretary had received no actual bridge or port proposal. I have seen no evidence of such a change myself, and I do not know who originated these statements or what purpose they serve. I should distinguish this circulating talk from verified town business and seek clarification without repeating it as fact.
